issue.title: [Bug] Command Code built-in: stealth/reflection models 400 on replayed turns — reasoning_content is not replayed via the API-key host
issue.body:
**What happens**

With the built-in `commandcode` provider (API key; host `api.commandcode.ai`), the stealth/reflection models fail on every turn that replays an assistant message through the Responses→Chat relay:

- `commandcode/stealth/cat-jam:free` — first turn 200; every later turn 400.
- `commandcode/reflection/beam:free` — same.
- `commandcode/stealth/glyph-cluster:free` — unaffected.

Seen through a client (Codex via `/v1/responses`, magpie 0.1.1276):

```
[System Error] {"error":{"code":null,"message":"Command Code: {\"error\":{\"message\":\"The stealth model could not complete the request.\",\"type\":\"provider_error\"}}","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

It is a fast deterministic 400 (~230 ms). Replaying the relay's Chat request shape directly against beam surfaces the real validation error:

```
Missing required parameter: 'messages[1].reasoning_content'. This model needs the reasoning of every earlier assistant message
```

**Minimal repro (single factor)**

Same chat body, only the assistant message differs:

- `[user, user]` → 200
- `[user, assistant]` → 400
- `[user, assistant + reasoning_content]` → 200 (both cat-jam and beam)

Other free models through the same relay replay assistant tool turns fine (`openrouter/free`, `opencode-go/longcat-2.5-preview-free`, `opencode-zen/glm-5.3-flash-free`), so the gap is specific to these Command Code models.

**Source reading**

`chatReplaysReasoning` in `internal/gateway/chat.go` (v0.1.1276):

```go
func chatReplaysReasoning(host, model string) bool {
	return strings.Contains(host, "deepseek") || strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(model), "deepseek") || host == provider.CommandCodePlanID
}
```

`buildHost` returns the plugin id only for plugin providers; the built-in provider returns `api.commandcode.ai`, so `replay` is false and `buildChat` never adds `reasoning_content` to the replayed assistant tool turns. The comment on `chatReplaysReasoning` says "Command Code's plugin, which replays it for a Go key as the built-in did to /alpha/generate" — it looks like the built-in's replay was scoped to the old `/alpha/generate` path, but the current built-in stealth/reflection models (served through `/provider/v1`) want it back too.

**Suggested direction**

Also replay for the Command Code built-in host (e.g. match `api.commandcode.ai`, or the `stealth/` / `reflection/` model prefixes), the way #1462 handled DeepSeek's variants.

**Workaround**

`magpie model disable commandcode/stealth/cat-jam:free commandcode/reflection/beam:free` removes them from the catalog and every group immediately (direct calls then 403). An exposure-level unpick (`magpie provider models commandcode -stealth/cat-jam:free ...`) is not enough: named group members are not filtered by the served list — `membersIn` only honors the disabled-models list. Note too that the 400 does not trigger group failover, so a group whose first member is cat-jam dies on its second turn.

Related: #1462 (DeepSeek rejects replayed tool turns without reasoning), #1765 (repeated 400s with no failover).

comments.body:
Delivered on `fix/commandcode-replay-reasoning` ([741237cf](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/741237cf), skygunner's fork, on upstream/main 1b039a3c), following your source reading: `chatReplaysReasoning` now says commandcode wherever it is served — the plugin id it already knew, and the built-in's own host `api.commandcode.ai` that matched nothing and had its turns replayed bare. The way #1462 did for DeepSeek's variants.

Red before: `TestCommandCodeHostReplaysReasoning` (the built-in host's replay off — your first-turn-200/turn-two-400 shape) and `TestCommandCodeReplayCarriesReasoningContent` (a replayed assistant tool turn went out with no `reasoning_content`); after, the reasoning the turn was given rides the tool turn, as the plugin's replay always carried it. A host that never asked for it (api.openai.com) is unchanged, and no reasoning is invented: the field is replayed only from what the turn actually carried.

Run: `go test ./internal/gateway -count=1` (one red, the known #3280 on this bash-as-sh machine), gofmt, go vet, windows/amd64 and darwin/arm64 builds.

## Result

I independently cherry-picked skygunner's `741237cf` onto current upstream main `9277c256`; it applies cleanly. This broad host-level fix is preferable to a model-specific exception.

Verification branch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/tree/codex/verify-2741-commandcode-reasoning (rebased commit `9966759a`).

## Evidence

- `TestCommandCodeHostReplaysReasoning` and `TestCommandCodeReplayCarriesReasoningContent` pass on the rebased patch (`go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestCommandCodeHostReplaysReasoning|TestCommandCodeReplayCarriesReasoningContent' -count=1`, 2.473s).
- `go vet ./internal/gateway`, native `go build ./...`, and Windows/amd64 `go build ./...` pass.
- `gofmt` and `git diff --check` are clean.

## Boundary

Not tried: a live Command Code key or an end-to-end stealth/reflection conversation. The exact reported replay shape is covered by the new regression.

This is independent verification of skygunner's patch, not a competing implementation. No code change appears necessary beyond landing that patch.

issue.title: privacy model: its download ignores Settings' Proxy (fails where a proxy is the only way out)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
# privacy model: its download ignores Settings' Proxy

## What happens

On a machine whose only way out is a proxy, Settings → Privacy's local model fails to turn on:

```
downloading pf-serve: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/releases/download/pf-v1/pf-serve-linux-amd64.zip:
Get "https://release-assets.githubusercontent.com/github-production-release-asset/…":
net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

Settings' Proxy is set (`socks5h://192.168.1.233:1081`) and works — the very same URL through it
downloads in 6 seconds. Turning the model on again fails the same way, this time as a plain
`dial tcp <github ip>:443: i/o timeout`, so the request never goes near the proxy.

The model (huggingface.co) would fail the same way on such a network, so the feature cannot be
turned on at all.

## Why

`internal/pii/fetch.go` builds its client at package init:

```go
var client = func() *http.Client {
	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	t.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 60 * time.Second
	return &http.Client{Transport: t}
}()
```

`netproxy.Install()` — which sets `http.DefaultTransport.Proxy = netproxy.Func`, the thing that makes
every other request of magpie's follow Settings' Proxy — runs later, from `main`
(`internal/cli/main.go`). The clone is made before it, so it keeps `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`,
which in the app and in the container has nothing to read. Both downloads therefore go direct,
whatever Settings say. (`source.Do` still asks mirrors when it can, but the zip's only mirror is
`gh-proxy`, which is behind `MAGPIE_MIRRORS=on`, so it changes nothing here.)

## Fix

`internal/update/update.go` already has the shape for exactly this:

```go
func proxied() http.RoundTripper {
	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	t.Proxy = netproxy.Func
	return netproxy.Dispatch(t)
}
```

so `internal/pii/fetch.go` can do the same (with `github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/netproxy`
imported):

```go
var client = func() *http.Client {
	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	t.Proxy = netproxy.Func // Settings' Proxy, as every other request of magpie's
	t.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 60 * time.Second
	return &http.Client{Transport: t}
}()
```

Then both downloads follow Settings' Proxy (and its LAN bypass), `MAGPIE_MIRRORS=on` still gives the
`gh-proxy` fallback, and the checksums stay as they are — a mirror or a proxy is only the way there.

## Workaround (no rebuild)

Put the two files where the download would have put them, then turn the model on again — it is
judged by what is on disk, so no restart is needed:

```
<cache>/privacy-filter/pf-v1-linux-amd64/   ← the zip's contents, pf-serve executable
<cache>/privacy-filter/privacy-filter-q8-80efc1803eda.gguf
```

where `<cache>` is `~/.cache/magpie` (app, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` respected) or `/config/cache/magpie`
(the container image). The zip is `pf-serve-linux-amd64.zip` from the `pf-v1` release
(sha256 `b172f39b2b5446cb92ef14f996b65157f5e1c0e4e673ee9c61a0214cc67c78af`); the model is
`privacy-filter-q8.gguf` at revision `935d8688`
(sha256 `80efc1803eda7c095a79741d2008c07e2e0a57b01bac8825fbeb448fd097998c`, 1637572192 bytes).

## Environment

magpie v0.1.1471, server edition (the container image: `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/config/cache`),
linux-amd64, behind a proxy-only network.

## Patch

```diff
diff --git a/internal/pii/fetch.go b/internal/pii/fetch.go
index ed23cb59..ee85637b 100644
--- a/internal/pii/fetch.go
+++ b/internal/pii/fetch.go
@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@ import (
 	"sync/atomic"
 	"time"
 
+	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/netproxy"
 	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/source"
 )
 
@@ -33,6 +34,9 @@ var dl struct {
 // whose server doesn't answer by the header timeout.
 var client = func() *http.Client {
 	t := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
+	// through Settings' Proxy as every other request of magpie's is: the
+	// clone is made before netproxy.Install sets it on http.DefaultTransport
+	t.Proxy = netproxy.Func
 	t.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 60 * time.Second
 	return &http.Client{Transport: t}
 }()
```
